Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The bug report summary says the core union operation fails to sort result nodes according to document order. The description uses an example with a XML document having
avaluebvalue
, and the XPath expression is string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A). According to the spec, when converting a node-set to string, the string value of the node first in document order should be returned, which would be the text from (avalue). The bug report says the actual value is "b", meaning the text under is returned, indicating the node-set returned by union isn't ordered by document order. The failing test tests union of /vendor[1]/contact[4] and /vendor[1]/contact[1], then expects "John" (some text presumably from contact[1]). This also relates to union result not being in document order. I tried looking at methods named union or getNodeset or similar in CoreOperationUnion and DOMModel but couldn't find useful methods, likely because relevant methods aren't named exactly like that. The TreeCompiler has a union method that returns a new CoreOperationUnion with the expressions passed, so CoreOperationUnion handles the union logic. We want to look inside CoreOperationUnion to see how union nodes are collected and returned: - How are nodes from input node sets combined? - Is there a sorting step ensuring document order? Given that union is meant to return nodes in document order with duplicates removed, absence of sorting will cause this issue. I will attempt to get the code snippet of CoreOperationUnion, particularly methods related to node-set evaluation or merging. I'll try CoreOperationUnion.computeNodes() or evaluateNodeset() or a method that returns the union set. If unavailable, try all methods of CoreOperationUnion to find the relevant one.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
